svg.text: 1 · SUM (Sony, soundcore): add every byte, keep the low 8 bits
Cheap, catches most single-byte errors, blind to swapped bytes.
2 · CRC = THE REMAINDER OF A DIVISION (no carries: subtract is XOR)
message 0xA0 = 10100000, divided by 1011 (x³ + x + 1), with three 0s appended
Treat the bits as a long binary number and divide by a fixed pattern.
The sender appends the remainder; the receiver divides
message+remainder and must get zero. Flip any bit, any burst shorter
than the CRC, or swap bytes, and the remainder changes. Real CRCs use
16-bit patterns and run a byte at a time with shifts – exactly the
3 · CRC-16/XMODEM (Samsung: poly 0x1021, start 0) — “find my buds, start”
header: 55 · control 5120 · command C007 · len 0 · fsn 0
OPO has none: RFCOMM's own checks already protect the bytes; brands add their own anyway for older links.
